result.title: A Better Critic Matters for Distribution Matching Distillation
result.comment: 35 pages, 16 figures. Project page and code: https://peppaking8.github.io/critic-matters/
result.summary: Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) trains a few-step student using the difference between a teacher's score and an online critic's estimate of the student distribution's score. We investigate what the critic needs, in capacity and in information, to provide a reliable training signal. On the capacity side, controlled experiments across seven SiT model sizes on ImageNet show that increasing teacher size while keeping a small critic fixed can degrade student quality and cause training collapse. Scaling the critic alongside the teacher, a strategy we call joint scaling, prevents collapse in our experiments and allows the student to benefit from larger teachers. On the information side, rather than forcing the critic to model a step-agnostic mixture of student outputs, we introduce a step-aware critic (STAC) that conditions on the student's generation step to estimate step-specific scores. Together, joint scaling and STAC consistently improve few-step distillation across class-conditional ImageNet generation, text-to-image generation with SDXL and FLUX.2, and text-to-video generation with Wan2.1.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 DMD 少步蒸馏中 critic 需要多少容量与信息：发现 critic 不随 teacher 扩展会导致崩溃，因而提出 joint scaling，并用按学生生成步条件化的 step-aware critic（STAC）替代步无关的混合分数估计。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按生成步条件化的评分器」及「步特定状态 vs 步无关混合」的对比，可能与 latent 推理轨迹中的逐步信用分配与监督信号设计相通，可供核查；但本文属扩散蒸馏，与 VLM 推理无直接联系。
